transcript: The heavy board member had taken his spectacles off his forehead and was holding them in his hand. I woke, said the proprietor, and went to the window, and the lamps went white. He turned his head from the harbour window and looked down the length of the table at Kiva. I've dreamed it eleven times since. Not often. Not on any night I could choose. Always with a fever, and always near a thing I can't name. And never once since 2611 when I didn't have my hand on this glass. The last was in the ninth month of last year. The seventeenth. In the evening. The seventeenth of the ninth month. Twenty past two. The bank in this harbour, falling into step. The pit. The lampman at Holloway. With a fever two nights. Who would not have it written.
